method: Fresh verifier and fresh adversarial-falsifier sub-agents, run in parallel in cycle 2 of the night of 2026-08-19/20, neither having drafted the story. Both independently fetched Stripe's and OpenRouter's own announcement pages; the verifier focused on establishing independent sourcing for the reported price, the falsifier tried to find a denial, a relay-not-independent pattern, or a stale/recirculated story. This story was opened as 'watching' on 2026-08-16 (see ledger notes 2026-08-16 through 2026-08-20) because every report traced to a single Bloomberg wire exclusive; today's on-the-record company announcements from both parties resolve that gate for the fact of the deal, though not for its price.
origin_items: data/raw/2026-08-19/techmeme.json (Bloomberg 'Stripe Agrees to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter; No Terms Disclosed', ~17:27 UTC, and New York Times/Erin Griffith item, ~18:00 UTC)
data/raw/2026-08-19/cnbc-technology.json ('Stripe to buy OpenRouter as fintech expands deeper into AI', ~20:10 UTC)

claims.text: Stripe has agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a New York-based startup that operates a marketplace/gateway routing requests across hundreds of third-party AI models
claims.reasoning: Confirmed directly from both parties' own on-the-record announcements published today: Stripe's newsroom post ('Stripe...today announced that it has agreed to acquire OpenRouter') and OpenRouter's own blog ('we are excited to announce that we are joining forces with Stripe'). Two independent Tier-0 primary sources, each confirming its own side of the transaction -- stronger than the single anonymous-sourced Bloomberg exclusive this story was held on since 2026-08-16.

claims.text: Neither company disclosed the deal's financial terms in its announcement
claims.reasoning: Both primary announcements omit a price figure; the verifier and falsifier sub-agents independently fetched both pages and confirmed neither states a number.

claims.text: Media reports on the price vary and are not confirmed by either company: Bloomberg first reported 'over $7 billion'; the New York Times later reported about $7.5 billion, split $1.5 billion to OpenRouter's founders and $6 billion to its investors, a figure CNBC's coverage attributes to the Times rather than its own reporting; other outlets have cited over $8 billion
claims.reasoning: The verifier and falsifier independently found a real, unreconciled spread (roughly $7B-$8B+, about a 14% range) across outlets, none corroborated by Stripe or OpenRouter. The falsifier specifically checked whether CNBC's $7.5B figure was independent or relayed and found CNBC's own framing attributes it to the New York Times ('the New York Times said the price tag is about $7.5 billion') rather than reporting it as CNBC's own sourcing -- a relay, not a second independent source on that specific number. Treated as disputed rather than confirmed at any single figure; the article states the range with attribution instead of asserting one number as fact, per verification.md's disagreement-downgrades-to-disputed rule.

claims.text: The deal is subject to customary closing conditions and had not closed as of the announcement, with closing expected in the coming weeks
claims.reasoning: Stated explicitly in OpenRouter's own announcement ('The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions. We expect to close in the coming weeks.'). Basis for the open_obligation flag on the ledger entry.

falsifier_notes: Searched specifically for a Stripe/OpenRouter denial or 'no comment' (found none -- the opposite, an affirmative on-the-record company announcement with a named CEO quote); checked whether today's NYT and CNBC coverage was independent reporting or a relay of Bloomberg's original 2026-08-16 exclusive (the deal-is-happening fact now traces to the companies' own primary announcements, not to Bloomberg, so this is moot for that claim; on the specific price figure, found CNBC relaying NYT rather than sourcing independently); checked for stale/recirculated dating (confirmed this is a genuine escalation -- anonymous-sourced rumor on 08-16 to on-the-record company confirmation on 08-19 -- not a republish); checked OpenRouter's public traction claims (8M users, 400+ models) for disputes and found none, though several outlets note the implied revenue multiple (roughly 50-140x) as aggressive analyst commentary, not a factual dispute. qz.com appeared in search results and was excluded as evidence per policy/discovery.yaml's blocked_evidence_domains list.
dedup_check: PYTHONPATH=pipeline python -m noiseless.run dedup-check --title "Stripe agrees to acquire OpenRouter" --url "https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-agrees-to-acquire-openrouter" returned exit 0 with a moderate match (score 0.5) against the existing stripe-openrouter-acquisition watching-state ledger entry (open since 2026-08-16) and a separate, coincidental moderate match against amd-taalas-acquisition (unrelated companies, title-similarity only on 'acquisition'/'AI'). Outcome: same story, existing slug -- this is the first publication of an already-open watching entry now that the evidence bar is met, not a new or follow-up article.
